hypotheses.text: LGMDR29 (SNUPN deficiency) exhibits an age-dependent weakness topography, wherein childhood-onset cases manifest purely proximal limb-girdle weakness whereas adult-onset cases present with proximo-distal and prominent axial weakness mimicking inclusion body myositis.
hypotheses.rationale: Early reports described SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy as a childhood-onset proximal limb-girdle disorder, but newer adult-onset pedigrees demonstrate combined distal, axial, and respiratory involvement, suggesting that clinical presentations vary significantly across the age spectrum.

evidence.text: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures.

source.quote: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures, although inter-individual variability in terms of severity even in individuals from the same family was found.

evidence.text: Two siblings with adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy presented with proximo-distal and axial weakness alongside early respiratory involvement, clinically reminiscent of inclusion body myositis.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement... We advise SNUPN testing in patients with late-onset proximo-distal and axial weakness with early respiratory impairment and features reminding inclusion body myositis (IBM).

hypotheses.text: Spinocerebellar ataxia/atrophy represents an allelic manifestation of SNUPN variants that can occur either as an asymptomatic neuroimaging sign or as an independent primary degenerative feature without overt limb weakness.
hypotheses.rationale: Initial cohorts suggested absence of primary CNS involvement, but recent functional and imaging data identify cerebellar Purkinje cell vulnerability and asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy in SNUPN variant carriers.

evidence.text: One adult-onset SNUPN patient showed asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI.

hypotheses.text: Primary myocardial damage and cardiomyopathy can precede skeletal muscle symptoms as the presenting manifestation in a subset of LGMDR29 patients.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior assertions held that SNUPN-related disease lacks primary cardiac involvement, but emerging clinical reports suggest myocardial damage may be the initial presenting sign prior to significant ambulation deficit.

evidence.text: LGMDR29 can present with myocardial damage as the initial clinical manifestation despite preserved motor developmental milestones.

hypotheses.text: Muscle MRI reveals a discriminatory selectivity pattern in SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy characterized by selective involvement of the paravertebral, vasti, gracilis, sartorius, and medial gastrocnemius muscles regardless of childhood or adult onset.
hypotheses.rationale: Establishing a consistent muscle MRI signature across both classic childhood-onset LGMD and atypical adult-onset proximo-distal presentations provides a reliable phenotypic discriminator against other LGMD subtypes and inclusion body myositis.

evidence.text: Childhood-onset SNUPN patients showed selective MRI fatty replacement of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal, and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and age distribution of subclinical or overt myocardial disease across all reported biallelic SNUPN individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether myocardial impairment is an under-recognized systemic manifestation across cohorts or an isolated feature of specific variant alleles will determine mandatory cardiology screening protocols in LGMDR29.

new_directions.question_text: Do N-terminal versus C-terminal SNUPN variants correlate with distinct phenotypes (e.g., pure limb-girdle vs. inclusion body myositis-like proximo-distal vs. spinocerebellar atrophy)?
new_directions.rationale: Variants reported in adult-onset IBM-like disease (p.Arg27Cys, p.Cys174Tyr) differ in location from C-terminal clusters reported in pediatric cohorts, indicating possible genotype-phenotype correlations.
